answer: Approximately 5.6% (1 of 18) of the original studies in the Experimental Economics replication project were conducted in the United Kingdom. The single UK original study is ee.13, "Deferred compensation in multiperiod labor contracts: an experimental study" (its replication was also run in the UK). All 18 EE original studies have a recorded experiment country (none missing), so the denominator is unambiguous: 1/18 = 0.0556 ≈ 5.56%. The second dataset (replication_success) independently confirms the count of 18 Experimental Economics studies but contains no country information and has no exact join key, so it plays only a count-consistency role.

payload.workflow: 1) Loaded dataset 1 (927 rows) and filtered to project=='ee' → 18 rows, verified 18 unique ids and 18 unique titles (no lab-level duplication; lab_id blank). 2) Counted rows with trimmed, case-insensitive experiment_country.o=='united kingdom' → 1 (ee.13). 3) Proportion = 1/18 = 0.0556 (5.56%) with denominator = all 18 EE original studies (no missing-country exclusions needed). 4) Wrote per-study audit listing to analysis/uk_proportion_ee_result.json and cross-checked EE count against dataset 2's 18 'Experimental Economics' rows (count-only match; no join key).
